header.userPrompt:
Feature: merchant names as implicit categorization rules (merchant-alias model), end to end.

Context: rules live in merchant_rule (action set_merchant|ignore, pattern CITEXT, merchant_id). Matching is in lib/api/shared ImportRuleMatcher (normalize = lowercase + strip non-alphanumerics, then substring contains; 3-char normalized floor; longest normalized pattern wins; ignore beats set_merchant) and RowRuleVerdict. Today a merchant only auto-matches a row if an explicit set_merchant rule exists, and the confirm-expense modal (web BankRowCreateExpenseForm) stores the merchant name as the pattern via a "Use original description as rule pattern" checkbox. That denormalizes the name (renaming a merchant leaves the rule stale) and ~60% of rules just duplicate the merchant name; it also silently creates a second overlapping rule when a row already matched one, and swallows rule-creation errors.

Goal: every merchant name matches implicitly; explicit set_merchant rules are only ALIASES for when the bank text differs from the name.

Engine:
1. In lib/api/shared, add one helper that, given explicit rules plus the user's merchants, returns the effective List[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]: explicit rules plus one virtual SetMerchant rule per merchant (pattern = merchant name, merchantId = that merchant). Reuse the existing length floor and longest-match/ignore precedence unchanged. Virtual rules are computed, never stored. An explicit rule duplicating a merchant-name virtual rule must not change the winner.
2. Route every merchant/verdict resolution for a row or description through this helper so matching includes merchant names: RowRuleVerdict callers, BankStatementReviewPage, StatementSuggestionsService and JevStatementSuggestionsService (selectRowsToResolve), ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction, TelegramExpenseAction, ParseReceiptAction, ReceiptsPage, ReconciliationMatcher/BankStatementAutoReconcilePage, BulkMerchantSetupPage, and the bank-row forms. Pass merchants where already loaded; load them where not.

UX (web BankRowCreateExpenseForm):
3. Remove the checkbox. The rule concept becomes an alias field shown ONLY when the resolved merchant's normalized name is NOT already a substring of this row's description (implicit matching won't catch future rows). In that case show an editable "Rule pattern" field defaulted to the row description; blank means do not create a rule. When the merchant name already matches the row, show a read-only note that future rows match automatically and create no rule.
4. If the row already matches an existing explicit rule, show it read-only ("Covered by rule: X") and offer no creation.
5. Create a rule only when the field is non-empty and its normalized value differs from the merchant name. Surface rule-creation errors inline instead of swallowing them; the expense must still be created independently of rule success.

Do NOT delete or migrate any existing rules; this PR is additive. Keep behavior identical for rows already matched by an explicit alias or ignore rule. Tests: unit-test the helper (name matches containing description; "CAFE DINDURRA" beats "CAFE"; ignore wins; <3-char names excluded; renamed merchant changes matching with no rule row). Avoid redundant action-level tests the reviewers would flag.
